<!-- REBASE-48K-20261102:BEGIN -->
## Current rebase and CI status (2026-11-02)

Head `840ddc2dab5e6bad4db7686e7d610a97a3310539` is rebased onto upstream main `23c6442cde7fb38230134ba0e3513ad2332aa5cf`. The patch is unchanged according to `git range-diff`.

Local validation: 4 real-ZMQ CPU regression tests and scoped pre-commit hooks passed; range-diff unchanged. No fresh GPU/model or performance result is claimed; earlier measurements below remain tied to their original revisions.

[Latest Base run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41402282474) (attempt 2) stops at **Require run-ci label (optional)**. The PR is Ready. A CI-authorized maintainer must add `run-ci` and issue `/tag-and-rerun-ci`; the author-requested retry ran but cannot grant the label.

[Repository-wide lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41402282458/job/125136503294) independently fails on `F821 logger` in the unchanged main XPU graph runner. [Upstream report and reproducer](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30980#issuecomment-6571123990). The PR-scoped local hooks passed; the full upstream check has not passed. Rebase after the main repair lands.

[Rebase validation and CI request](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46820#issuecomment-6570996215).
<!-- REBASE-48K-20261102:END -->

## Problem and root cause

Auxiliary KV-metrics publication runs in the scheduler loop. A missing or slow PUSH-socket receiver can exhaust its queue; the default blocking `sock_send` then stalls request progress. This remains present on main `8a455f1`.

Our archived GLM-5.2 run `c44a` hung at this call (py-spy, October 9, ledger R001); `c44b` advanced past it with nonblocking metrics. Later stack throughput is not evidence for this patch, and the historical throughput runs used simulated MTP acceptance.

## Fix

Send auxiliary KV metrics with `zmq.NOBLOCK`, catch only queue-unavailable `zmq.Again`, and warn once per publisher. Keep KV-event publishing on its existing separate path. Unexpected socket errors still propagate. A healthy receiver continues to receive the serialized metrics after draining a full queue.

## Validation

Registered CPU tests use real ZeroMQ sockets for an unbound receiver, full high-water mark and recovery, plus closed-socket and non-EAGAIN controls. These tests do not require GPUs or models.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_kv_metrics_backpressure.py
pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-commit --files python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/kv_events_publisher.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_kv_metrics_backpressure.py
```

Local result: **4 passed**; all applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

## Review scope and CI

This change deliberately treats auxiliary KV metrics as best-effort telemetry: a full queue drops the current sample and warns once, so telemetry backpressure cannot stop request progress. Durable KV-event publication remains on its existing separate path. Please review this policy and the bounded logging behavior.

Author-side validation is complete for this CPU/socket-only change at `82176e70284c8d67b41de74b8e8005d148e57c8b`: the four real-ZMQ regression cases and applicable local pre-commit hooks pass, and upstream lint/title checks pass. No GPU or model execution is needed to validate this socket contract; no throughput improvement is claimed.

Ready for review. Upstream CPU test execution still requires the maintainer-controlled `run-ci` label; the existing gated/skipped test workflows are not claimed as passing. Maintainer review and required upstream checks remain merge requirements.

@@ -1,5 +1,6 @@
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import logging
 import time
 from dataclasses import dataclass
 from typing import (
@@ -21,6 +22,8 @@
 from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import hook_custom_types, sock_send
 from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
 
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
 if TYPE_CHECKING:
     from sglang.srt.mem_cache.base_prefix_cache import BasePrefixCache
 
@@ -52,6 +55,7 @@ class SchedulerKvEventsPublisher:
     get_stats: Callable
     enable_kv_cache_events: bool = False
     kv_event_publisher: Any = None
+    metrics_drop_warned: bool = False
 
     def __post_init__(self) -> None:
         self.init_kv_events(self.kv_events_config)
@@ -87,7 +91,18 @@ def emit_kv_metrics(self):
         )
 
         if not self.send_metrics_from_scheduler.closed:
-            sock_send(self.send_metrics_from_scheduler, kv_metrics)
+            # Auxiliary telemetry must not stall the scheduler when the receiver
+            # is unavailable or cannot keep up. KV events use a separate publisher.
+            try:
+                sock_send(
+                    self.send_metrics_from_scheduler, kv_metrics, flags=zmq.NOBLOCK
+                )
+            except zmq.Again:
+                if not self.metrics_drop_warned:
+                    logger.warning(
+                        "KV metrics receiver unavailable or queue full; dropping auxiliary metrics"
+                    )
+                    self.metrics_drop_warned = True
 
     def local_kv_event_sources(self, block_size: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
         if self.kv_event_publisher is None:

@@ -0,0 +1,102 @@
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import zmq
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import sock_recv
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler_components import kv_events_publisher as module
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=1, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestKvMetricsBackpressure(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.context = zmq.Context()
+        self.sender = self.context.socket(zmq.PUSH)
+        self.sender.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 0)
+        self.sender.setsockopt(zmq.SNDHWM, 1)
+        # Bound failures on unpatched code; production uses an infinite timeout.
+        self.sender.setsockopt(zmq.SNDTIMEO, 100)
+        self.addCleanup(self.context.destroy, linger=0)
+        with patch.object(module.SchedulerKvEventsPublisher, "init_kv_events"):
+            self.publisher = module.SchedulerKvEventsPublisher(
+                kv_events_config=None,
+                tree_cache=None,
+                send_metrics_from_scheduler=self.sender,
+                max_running_requests=16,
+                max_total_num_tokens=1024,
+                get_stats=lambda: SimpleNamespace(
+                    num_running_reqs=SimpleNamespace(total=2),
+                    num_queue_reqs=SimpleNamespace(total=3),
+                    token_usage=0.25,
+                    cache_hit_rate=0.5,
+                ),
+                enable_kv_cache_events=True,
+            )
+        parallel = patch.object(
+            module, "get_parallel", return_value=SimpleNamespace(dp_rank=2)
+        )
+        parallel.start()
+        self.addCleanup(parallel.stop)
+
+    def receiver(self):
+        receiver = self.context.socket(zmq.PULL)
+        receiver.setsockopt(zmq.RCVHWM, 1)
+        receiver.setsockopt(zmq.RCVTIMEO, 1000)
+        receiver.bind("inproc://kv-metrics-test")
+        self.sender.connect("inproc://kv-metrics-test")
+        return receiver
+
+    def test_unbound_receiver_drops_and_warns_once(self):
+        self.sender.connect("inproc://missing-receiver")
+        # Exhaust even the queue allocated for a not-yet-bound inproc peer.
+        for _ in range(4096):
+            try:
+                self.sender.send(b"queued", zmq.NOBLOCK)
+            except zmq.Again:
+                break
+        else:
+            self.fail("Socket did not apply its high-water mark")
+        with patch.object(module.logger, "warning") as warning:
+            self.publisher.emit_kv_metrics()
+            self.publisher.emit_kv_metrics()
+        warning.assert_called_once()
+
+    def test_full_queue_recovers_when_receiver_drains(self):
+        receiver = self.receiver()
+        queued = 0
+        for _ in range(4096):
+            try:
+                self.sender.send(b"queued", zmq.NOBLOCK)
+                queued += 1
+            except zmq.Again:
+                break
+        else:
+            self.fail("Socket did not apply its high-water mark")
+        with patch.object(module.logger, "warning") as warning:
+            self.publisher.emit_kv_metrics()
+        warning.assert_called_once()
+        for _ in range(queued):
+            self.assertEqual(receiver.recv(), b"queued")
+        self.assertTrue(self.sender.poll(1000, zmq.POLLOUT))
+        self.publisher.emit_kv_metrics()
+        metrics = sock_recv(receiver)
+        self.assertIsInstance(metrics, module.KvMetrics)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics.request_active_slots, 2)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics.kv_active_blocks, 256)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics.data_parallel_rank, 2)
+
+    def test_closed_socket_is_ignored(self):
+        self.sender.close()
+        self.publisher.emit_kv_metrics()
+
+    def test_other_socket_errors_are_not_hidden(self):
+        with patch.object(module, "sock_send", side_effect=zmq.ZMQError(zmq.EINVAL)):
+            with self.assertRaises(zmq.ZMQError):
+                self.publisher.emit_kv_metrics()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
